section_title: Can people harm God’s children and still honor His house?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 36 Then the LORD said to me: “Son of man, will you pass judgment against Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their abominations. 37 For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols. They have even sacrificed their children, whom they bore to Me, in the fire as food for their idols. 38 They have also done this to Me: On that very same day, they defiled My sanctuary and profaned My Sabbaths. 39 On the very day they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered My sanctuary to profane it. Yes, they did this inside My house.

40 Furthermore, you sisters sent messengers for men who came from afar; and behold, when they arrived, you bathed for them, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewelry. 41 You sat on a couch of luxury with a table spread before it, on which you had set My incense and My oil, 42 accompanied by the sound of a carefree crowd. Drunkards were brought in from the desert along with men from the rabble, who put bracelets on your wrists and beautiful crowns on your head. 43 Then I said of her who had grown old in adulteries: ‘Now let them use her as a prostitute, for that is all she is!’ 44 And they slept with her as with a prostitute; they slept with Oholah and Oholibah, those lewd women.

45 But righteous men will sentence them to the punishment of those who commit adultery and bloodshed, because they are adulteresses with blood on their hands. 46 This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Bring a mob against them and consign them to terror and plunder. 47 The mob will stone them and cut them down with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn down their houses. 48 So I will put an end to indecency in the land, and all the women will be admonished not to imitate your behavior. 49 They will repay you for your indecency, and you will bear the consequences of your sins of idolatry. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.’”

context_lines: The Lord brings both sisters together under the accusation. Their idolatry includes the killing of children who belonged to Him. On the same day they slaughter those children, they enter His sanctuary.

The scene then returns to the sisters welcoming visitors, decorating themselves, and preparing a luxurious setting. The Lord’s incense and oil are set before the guests. What belongs to Him has been drawn into their unfaithfulness.

The closing scene announces judgment for adultery and bloodshed. The cities’ houses will burn, their children will be killed, and their conduct will become a warning. The conclusion repeats the purpose of the confrontation: they will know that He is the Lord.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/ezekiel/23.htm) emphasizes the immediate contradiction between idolatry and murder and then entering the temple. [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ezekiel/23.htm) reads the chapter as a call to repentance rather than confidence in one’s own righteousness.

Readings differ over the righteous men in verse 45. The [USCCB notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/ezekiel/23) apply the description to the executioners acting as agents of the Lord’s judgment. [Cambridge](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/cambridge/ezekiel/23.htm) understands righteous judges within the story’s courtroom picture, without identifying them as the nations that carry out the actual destruction. Neither reading turns the invading nations into a model of moral perfection.
god_plan_lines: [First Corinthians 10:14–22](https://biblehub.com/bsb/1_corinthians/10.htm) brings the issue of divided worship into the life of the church. Paul tells believers to flee idolatry and explains that sharing in the Lord’s table cannot be joined with sharing in the table of demons.

Paul does not explicitly quote this passage. The larger connection is that worship involves belonging and participation, not a ceremony that cancels out another allegiance. Ezekiel exposes people entering God’s sanctuary while persisting in idol worship; Paul calls those who share in Christ to an undivided loyalty to Him.
